blocks.text: The major portion of sulfur, around 85 per cent, is used to produce sulfuric acid. The molecule has a tetrahedral structure with two S-O (hydroxyl) and two S=O bonds (Figure 12.11).

blocks.alt: Left: structure of H2SO4, S with two double-bonded O atoms above and two OH groups below. Red double arrows give the bond lengths: S=O 142.2 pm, S-O 157.4 pm and O-H 97 pm. Right: a ball-and-stick view with a yellow S ball in the centre, four red O balls and two white H balls on the lower O atoms.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.11: Structure of H2SO4 (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.11).
